title: Beyond Similarity: Heterogeneous Graph Learning for Multi-Objective Food Substitution in Charitable Food Agencies
abstract: arXiv:2608.21979v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Charitable food agencies play an important role in alleviating food insecurity by distributing donated food to people in need. However, they rely on ad hoc in-kind donations and often face shortages of specific foods, so they offer substitutes. A good food substitution requires matching household preferences, nutritional needs, and item similarity. Agencies have limited direct records of consumption behavior due to resource constraints, making it challenging to make an appropriate substitution decision that meets multiple criteria. In this study, we propose a heterogeneous graph neural network (HeteroGNN), a source-grounded recommendation framework for food substitution in charitable food agencies. We first build a unified relational graph from large-scale public data sources, combining household behavior on food consumption and food nutrient information in the United States (US) context. translated_title: 超越相似性：面向慈善食品机构多目标食品替代的异构图学习
translated_abstract: 慈善食品机构通过向有需要的人分发捐赠食品，在缓解食品不安全方面发挥着重要作用。然而，它们依赖临时的实物捐赠，常常面临特定食品短缺，因此提供替代品。一个好的食品替代需要匹配家庭偏好、营养需求和物品相似性。由于资源限制，机构对消费行为的直接记录有限，这使得做出满足多重标准的适当替代决策变得具有挑战性。在本研究中，我们提出了一种异构图神经网络（HeteroGNN），一种基于来源的推荐框架，用于慈善食品机构中的食品替代。我们首先从大规模公共数据源构建一个统一的关系图，结合美国背景下家庭食品消费行为和食品营养信息。我们将替代推荐视为一个多目标优化问题，并利用异构图学习来捕捉不同实体之间的复杂关系。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于异构图神经网络的推荐框架，通过整合家庭消费和营养数据，解决慈善食品机构中多目标食品替代的挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a heterogeneous graph neural network-based recommendation framework that integrates household consumption and nutrition data to address the challenge of multi-objective food substitution in charitable food agencies.
